page: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Dlsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8). The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.28 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations are relatively limited. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is categorized as weak at 3908.06, and the Passmark memory score is also weak at 1647.88. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show weak performance, with read-only large block transfers at 36.43 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 25.65 GB/sec. Redis SET operations also register in the weak tier at 5.63 million operations per second.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2 and lack of local storage, the D4ls_v6 is positioned as a compute-oriented option for workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for single-threaded tasks, basic web serving (achieving an average static web serving throughput of 7.63 GB/sec), and light text processing. It can also handle small-scale LLM inference, processing 135M model prompts at 493.43 tokens per second. The hardware profile offers a cost-efficient entry point for dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources where memory capacity and high multi-threaded memory bandwidth are secondary requirements.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression.
